def draw_test_members(table):
    """Name the test members: TEST_FRACTION of each half, by member, from a
    RandomState created here from RNG_SEED (a re-run draws the same)."""
    rng = np.random.RandomState(RNG_SEED)
    test_members = []
    for _, half in table.groupby('forcing_variant'):
        hold = GroupShuffleSplit(
            n_splits=1, test_size=TEST_FRACTION, random_state=rng
        )
        _, held = next(hold.split(half, groups=half['member_id']))
        test_members += sorted(half.iloc[held]['member_id'].unique())
    return test_members

def fit_transforms(rows, years=YEARS):
    """Fit on `rows` ONLY: per series, a degree-FORCED_DEG polynomial in
    year through the ensemble mean of `rows`; and the wet threshold, the
    WET_QUANTILE of the pooled detrended precipitation of `rows`."""
    curves = {}
    for anom, raw in ANOMALIES.items():
        ens_mean = rows.groupby('winter')[raw].mean().reindex(years)
        coef = np.polyfit(years, ens_mean.values, FORCED_DEG)
        curves[anom] = pd.Series(np.polyval(coef, years), index=years)
    curve = curves['prect_anom'].reindex(rows['winter']).values
    prect_anom = pd.Series(rows['prect_winter_mm_day'].values - curve)
    return dict(
        curves=curves, wet_threshold=float(prect_anom.quantile(WET_QUANTILE))
    )


def apply_transforms(rows, tf):
    """Subtract the fitted curves and label `wet` against the fitted
    threshold, on any rows (held-out ones included). Fits nothing."""
    out = rows.copy()
    for anom, raw in ANOMALIES.items():
        curve = tf['curves'][anom].reindex(out['winter']).values
        out[anom] = out[raw].values - curve
    out['wet'] = (out['prect_anom'] > tf['wet_threshold']).astype(int)
    return out

Why not test the correlation with year
The correlation of the anomaly with year is zero by construction for any

DECADE_TOL = 3.0
d = table[is_train]
decade = (d["winter"] // 10) * 10
for anom, raw in ANOMALIES.items():
    r = d[raw].corr(d["winter"])
    print(
        f"corr({raw:20s}, year) = {r:+.3f}   "
        "(the forced trend in the raw series, training members)"
    )
removal_ok, n_tests = True, 0
for anom in ANOMALIES:
    g = d.groupby(decade)[anom]
    z = g.mean() / (d[anom].std() / np.sqrt(g.size()))
    worst = z.abs().idxmax()
    ok = bool((z.abs() <= DECADE_TOL).all())
    removal_ok &= ok
    n_tests += len(z)
    print(
        f"{anom:12s} decade-mean anomaly in standard errors: worst {z[worst]:+.2f} "
        f"(the {worst}s) · tolerance ±{DECADE_TOL:.0f} → {'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}"
    )
false_alarm = 1 - (1 - 2 * norm.sf(DECADE_TOL)) ** n_tests
verdict = (
    "PASS"
    if removal_ok
    else "FAIL — a forced path survived; change FORCED_DEG"
)
print(
    f"forced-response removal: {verdict}   ({n_tests} decade means; chance a "
    f"correct removal trips the tolerance somewhere ≈ {false_alarm:.0%})"
)

NWS Boulder’s sign for east of the Divide is positive — warmer autumn Pacific, wetter winter — and, for La Niña, the opposite (wetter) for
the northwest and north-central mountains, part of the box’s west column. Its El Niño-wet half is stated mainly for late
winter and spring, of which DJF holds only February; its La Niña-dry half for “the entire cold season”, which DJF is part of. Read the

line: do the members share a
sign? The

line says whether the mean is distinguishable from zero. Stagge et al. set the observed context: over a
climatological model, “the ENSO term explained an additional 2% of total variance” in their regional model, a share of
variance across gauges, which they say “should be viewed in the context of extreme spatial and elevation precipitation differences”, and their northern dipole model (“North–Wyoming”) is bounded
by 41.2° to 45.5° N. By latitude the Front Range, at about 38.5–40.5° N, falls outside the North–Wyoming model and sits mostly between the poles, its northern edge just past 40° N; and in the
northern pole the sign is reversed, with “increased winter precipitation during La Niña events”.

text/plain.content:
def wet_by_bin(rows, edges):
    """Wet rate per Niño 3.4 bin (the outer edges opened to ±inf, so
    edges fitted on one set of rows apply to any other), with a binomial
    standard error, the distance from these rows' own base rate in those
    errors, and a chi-square test of wet against bin.
    Returns (table, chi2, p, dof)."""
    e = np.array(edges, dtype=float)
    e[0], e[-1] = -np.inf, np.inf
    b = pd.cut(rows['nino34_anom'], e)
    base = rows['wet'].mean()
    t = rows.groupby(b, observed=True)['wet'].agg(['mean', 'size'])
    t.columns = ['wet_rate', 'n']
    t['binomial_se'] = np.sqrt(t['wet_rate'] * (1 - t['wet_rate']) / t['n'])
    t['(rate - base) / se'] = (t['wet_rate'] - base) / t['binomial_se']
    t.index.name = 'nino34_anom bin (K)'
    chi2, p, dof, _ = chi2_contingency(pd.crosstab(b, rows['wet']))
    return t, float(chi2), float(p), int(dof)

def wet_by_bin(rows, edges):
    """Wet rate per Niño 3.4 bin (the outer edges opened to ±inf, so
    edges fitted on one set of rows apply to any other), with a binomial
    standard error, the distance from these rows' own base rate in those
    errors, and a chi-square test of wet against bin.
    Returns (table, chi2, p, dof)."""
    e = np.array(edges, dtype=float)
    e[0], e[-1] = -np.inf, np.inf
    b = pd.cut(rows['nino34_anom'], e)
    base = rows['wet'].mean()
    t = rows.groupby(b, observed=True)['wet'].agg(['mean', 'size'])
    t.columns = ['wet_rate', 'n']
    t['binomial_se'] = np.sqrt(t['wet_rate'] * (1 - t['wet_rate']) / t['n'])
    t['(rate - base) / se'] = (t['wet_rate'] - base) / t['binomial_se']
    t.index.name = 'nino34_anom bin (K)'
    chi2, p, dof, _ = chi2_contingency(pd.crosstab(b, rows['wet']))
    return t, float(chi2), float(p), int(dof)
